```
export class LRUCache<T> {
  private cache = new Map<string, { value: T; expiresAt: number }>()
  private maxSize: number
  constructor(maxSize: number = 100) { this.maxSize = maxSize }
  get(key: string): T | undefined {
    const entry = this.cache.get(key)
    if (!entry) return undefined
    if (Date.now() > entry.expiresAt) { this.cache.delete(key); return undefined }
    this.cache.delete(key); this.cache.set(key, entry)
    return entry.value
  }
  set(key: string, value: T, ttlMs: number = 60000): void {
    if (this.cache.size >= this.maxSize) {
      const firstKey = this.cache.keys().next().value
      if (firstKey !== undefined) this.cache.delete(firstKey)
    }
    this.cache.set(key, { value, expiresAt: Date.now() + ttlMs })
  }
}

```

The `src/cache.ts` module implements a generic `LRUCache<T>` — a least-recently-used in-memory cache with TTL (time-to-live) support.

**What it does:**
- Stores key/value pairs in a `Map` where each entry also records an `expiresAt` timestamp.
- `get(key)` retrieves a value if present and not expired, and refreshes its recency by re-inserting it at the end of the map (making it the most-recently-used).
- `set(key, value, ttlMs)` inserts/updates an entry with a default TTL of 60,000 ms (60 seconds).

**Eviction strategy:**
- LRU (Least Recently Used). When the cache reaches `maxSize` (default 100) on a `set`, it evicts the first key in the map — the least-recently-used entry — before inserting the new one.

**On key expiration:**
- When `get` is called on an expired entry, the entry is deleted from the cache and `undefined` is returned. Expired entries are only purged lazily, i.e., when they are accessed via `get`; they are not cleaned up by a background process.

**Summary:** A bounded LRU cache with per-entry TTL. It evicts the least-recently-used item when full, and lazily removes and reports expired entries as `undefined` on access.
